classified_spans.text:
Here is my analysis of the `.gitignore` changes in PR #27:

---

## REMOVED Lines

**[CRITICAL] `scripts/` directory removed from ignore**
The old `.gitignore` ignored the entire `scripts/` directory. The PR removes this line entirely with no replacement. If `scripts/` contains private or local-only tooling, those files could now be accidentally committed. However, if the intent is to start tracking shared scripts, this is deliberate. Needs confirmation from the author on whether `scripts/` contents are meant to be public.

**[INFO] `*.pyo` and `*.pyd` replaced by `*.py[cod]` glob**
The old file listed `*.pyc`, `*.pyo`, `*.pyd` individually. The new file uses `*.py[cod]`, which covers all three in one pattern. Functionally equivalent -- no coverage lost.

**[WARNING] `sample_sessions/` broadened to only ignore subdirectories**
The old rule ignored the entire `sample_sessions/` directory. The PR narrows this to `sample_sessions/private/` and `sample_sessions/generated/`. This means files directly in `sample_sessions/` and any non-private/non-generated subdirectories will now be tracked. The CLAUDE.md documents `sample_sessions/` as a project directory for "Sample JSONL files for testing," so tracking the public fixtures is likely intentional. But any sensitive session data in other subdirectories would get committed.

**[INFO] `*.swp` moved, not removed**
The `*.swp` pattern was under "# OS" before and is now under "# IDE and editor files." Still present -- no issue.

---

## ADDED Lines

**[INFO] Local/private data section -- reasonable**
`Backup/`, `reports/`, `benchmark-results/`, `evaluation-results/`, `priority.csv`, `*.ter-report.html`, `*.benchmark.json`, `*.analysis.json` -- these are project-specific generated/local data patterns. All sensible for a tool that produces reports and benchmarks.

**[INFO] Python tooling caches -- standard**
`*$py.class`, `.ruff_cache/`, `.hypothesis/` -- standard additions for a Python project using ruff and hypothesis.

**[INFO] `env/` added**
Adds the `env/` virtualenv directory name alongside `.venv/`, `venv/`, `ENV/`. Common pattern, good to have.

**[INFO] Packaging extras -- standard**
`pip-wheel-metadata/` -- standard for modern pip workflows.

**[INFO] Coverage and test tooling -- standard**
`.coverage.*`, `coverage.xml`, `.tox/`, `.nox/` -- all standard Python testing patterns.

**[INFO] Type checking and profiling -- standard**
`.dmypy.json`, `dmypy.json` (mypy daemon), `*.prof` (profiling output) -- good additions.

**[INFO] Documentation build output -- standard**
`site/`, `docs/_build/` -- standard for mkdocs/sphinx builds.

**[INFO] Editor files expanded -- reasonable**
`*.swo`, `*~`, `.project`, `.pydevproject` -- covers vim backup files and Eclipse/PyDev project files.

**[INFO] OS files expanded -- reasonable**
`Desktop.ini` for Windows -- sensible given the project runs on Windows.

**[INFO] Temp/log files expanded -- reasonable**
`*.temp`, `*.bak`, `*.log` -- common transient file patterns.

**[INFO] `!.env.example` negation -- good practice**
Allows `.env.example` to be tracked while still ignoring all other `.env.*` files. This is a best practice for documenting required environment variables.

---

## Overly Broad Patterns

**[WARNING] `*.log` could suppress tracked log files**
The `*.log` pattern will ignore any file ending in `.log` anywhere in the repo. If the project ever has intentional `.log` files (e.g., sample log fixtures for testing), they would be silently excluded. The two `watch_log.jsonl` files currently shown as untracked in git status use the `.jsonl` extension, so they are unaffected. But worth noting.

**[WARNING] `*.bak` is broad but generally safe**
Backup files should typically not be tracked. Low risk.

**[INFO] `.claude/` is still ignored**
This means any `.claude/settings.json` or hooks configuration is local-only. This is the existing behavior and unchanged by the PR -- just noting it for awareness.

---

## Summary

| Severity | Count | Key Items |
|----------|-------|-----------|
| CRITICAL | 1 | `scripts/` no longer ignored -- verify intent |
| WARNING  | 2 | `sample_sessions/` narrowed (verify no sensitive data leaks); `*.log` is broad |
| INFO     | 12 | Standard Python gitignore improvements, all reasonable |

The PR modernizes the `.gitignore` into a comprehensive, well-organized Python template. The one item requiring author confirmation is the removal of `scripts/` from the ignore list. The narrowing of `sample_sessions/` looks intentional per the comment in the new file but should be verified against what currently exists in that directory.
